error.admin_login_name: The Ampio server and the name entered disagree about which account this is. not_configured_both.title: Ampio Designer rows this integration cannot use

confirm.title: Fix these rows in Ampio Designer
confirm.description:
The Ampio server serves Designer rows that this integration cannot use, and it left every one of them out.

Some objects point at no module output. This integration drives an object through that pointer, so it cannot read or control them, and their entities are gone from Home Assistant.

Ampio object ids ({object_count}):

{objects}

Ampio Designer clears the pointer when an object's Matter checkbox is unchecked and saved, and writes it back when the box is checked and saved. Open each object above in Designer, check its Matter box, and save. An entity that comes back as the same type comes back within seconds with the entity id, the name and the area it had, because Home Assistant kept its record. Checking the box also re-reads the object's type from the module record, so a relay can come back as a light where it was a switch, or as a switch where it was a light, and that entity registers under its new type as a new entity, with a new id and no history.

Some MAC addresses are carried by more than one module. Every frame on the Ampio bus is addressed by that MAC, so this integration cannot tell those modules apart and leaves them out of its module list.

Shared MAC addresses ({module_count}), each with the Designer device ids that carry it:

{modules}

Open each device in Designer, give it its own MAC address, and save. Match the devices by MAC rather than by position, because Designer numbers the rows of its device list by position and a deleted device leaves every number below the gap one short of the real device id.

Submit closes this notice and changes nothing, in Home Assistant or on the Ampio server. The notice comes back while the Designer project still reads this way.

not_configured_modules.title: Ampio modules sharing one MAC address

confirm.title: Give each Ampio module its own MAC address
confirm.description:
The Ampio server serves MAC addresses that more than one module carries. Every frame on the Ampio bus is addressed by that MAC, so this integration cannot tell those modules apart and leaves them out of its module list. Those modules carry no name, model or firmware version from Designer in Home Assistant, and the entities that need a module's own record, such as its buzzer and its panel controls, are not built.

Shared MAC addresses ({module_count}), each with the Ampio Designer device ids that carry it:

{modules}

Open each device in Designer, give it its own MAC address, and save. Match the devices by MAC rather than by position, because Designer numbers the rows of its device list by position and a deleted device leaves every number below the gap one short of the real device id. Refresh the Designer page afterwards and check that the new MAC stuck, because Designer can drop a MAC edit without saying so.

Submit closes this notice and changes nothing, in Home Assistant or on the Ampio server. The notice comes back while the Designer project still reads this way.

not_configured_objects.title: Ampio objects with no module output

confirm.title: Restore these Ampio objects in Ampio Designer
confirm.description:
The Ampio server serves objects that point at no module output. This integration drives an object through that pointer, so it cannot read or control them, and their entities are gone from Home Assistant.

Ampio object ids ({object_count}):

{objects}

Ampio Designer clears the pointer when an object's Matter checkbox is unchecked and saved, and writes it back when the box is checked and saved. Open each object above in Designer, check its Matter box, and save. An entity that comes back as the same type comes back within seconds with the entity id, the name and the area it had, because Home Assistant kept its record. Checking the box also re-reads the object's type from the module record, so a relay can come back as a light where it was a switch, or as a switch where it was a light. That entity registers under its new type as a new entity, with a new id and no history, so check whatever named the old one.

If you wanted an object gone, delete it in Designer instead. This notice drops it once the Ampio server pushes its next change, or when Home Assistant next starts, and the repair titled "Ampio records to clean up", or "Ampio records to check" on a standard account, then offers the records it left behind.

Submit closes this notice and changes nothing, in Home Assistant or on the Ampio server. The notice comes back while the Designer project still reads this way.

confirm.title: Delete the stale Ampio records
confirm.description:
Home Assistant still lists Ampio devices or entities that the Ampio server no longer accounts for on the account this integration uses:

{names}

Submit to delete these records from Home Assistant. Automations and dashboards that name them stop working. Nothing changes on the Ampio server. After the reload that follows, an object the Ampio server still serves comes back under the module it belongs to now.

If the account's access was narrowed in the Ampio app, do not submit. Restore the access in the app and reload the integration, and the records that access covers come back.

buzz_pattern.name: Play a buzzer pattern
buzz_pattern.description: Sounds a two-step sequence on a panel's buzzer. Each cycle plays the first tone, then the second. Tone 0 is silence, so three pips are one tone, one silent step, and three cycles.

tone.name: Tone
tone.description: Pitch of the first step, 0 to 31. Tone 6 is the loudest, and tone 0 is silence.

seconds.name: Length
seconds.description: How long the first step sounds, in seconds, up to 655.35.

tone2.name: Second tone
tone2.description: Pitch of the second step. Leave it at 0 for a silent gap.

seconds2.name: Second length
seconds2.description: How long the second step lasts, in seconds, up to 655.35.

cycles.name: Cycles
cycles.description: How many times to repeat the two steps, up to 254. 0 repeats until you turn the siren off.

delay.name: Delay
delay.description: How long to wait before the first step, in seconds, up to 655.35.

lock_touch.name: Lock a panel's touch fields
lock_touch.description: Makes an Ampio touch panel ignore every touch for a time. A locked field reports nothing at all, not even the press. Every lock expires, and the longest single lock is 655.35 seconds.

seconds.name: Length
seconds.description: How long the panel ignores touches, in seconds, from 0.01 to 655.35.

send_notification.name: Send a notification to the Ampio app
send_notification.description: Pushes a message to every user of the Ampio mobile app on this installation. The Ampio server answers on no topic, so a successful call means the message was sent and not that it arrived. A message cannot contain a slash: the server reads what follows one as a user name and drops the rest.

message.name: Message
message.description: The text the app shows. Spaces and accented characters arrive unchanged, but a slash is not allowed.

set_backlight_fields.name: Color backlight touch fields
set_backlight_fields.description: Colors the named touch fields of an Ampio panel's icon backlight, rather than the whole surface, and leaves the panel's Backlight entity reporting the color it already had.

fields.name: Fields
fields.description: The 1-based touch field numbers to color.

rgbw_color.name: Color
rgbw_color.description: The RGBW color to send to the named fields.

set_roller_lock.name: Set roller lock
set_roller_lock.description: Holds or releases one or both directions of a cover's roller lock. Only the Ampio administrator account can send this, because the lock frame rides the raw CAN tree.

direction.name: Direction
direction.description: The travel direction to lock or release: opening, closing, or both.

blocked.name: Blocked
blocked.description: On to hold the direction, off to release it.

set_status_fields.name: Color status light touch fields
set_status_fields.description: Colors the named touch fields of an Ampio panel's status indicator, rather than the whole surface, and leaves the panel's Status light entity reporting the color it already had.

fields.name: Fields
fields.description: The 1-based touch field numbers to color.

rgb_color.name: Color
rgb_color.description: The RGB color to send to the named fields.
